literal: While it is tender, a thorny tree, let one destroy; those who remove [it], [their] hand it will hurt, when [it has] hardened.
translation: Cut down a thorny tree while it is still young; if left to grow thick and mature, it will wound the hands of those who try to fell it.
modern: முள்மரத்தை அது இளமையாக இருக்கும்போதே வெட்டி அழிக்க வேண்டும்; அது முதிர்ந்து வளர்ந்துவிட்டால், அதனை வெட்டி அழிப்பவர்களின் கையை அது காயப்படுத்தும்.
explanation: This couplet uses the metaphor of a thorny tree to explain how to handle growing threats or enemies. When a thorny plant is young and tender, it can be easily removed without causing any harm. However, if it is allowed to grow, mature, and harden, its sharp thorns will injure the hands of those who try to clear it. Similarly, hostile forces or problems should be resolved in their early stages before they become powerful enough to cause damage when challenged.
